text:
Maria: Quick follow-up to the ingress failover RFC — we need to decide ownership boundaries for streaming failover. specifically: when ingress hands a stream to a fallback upstream, who owns resume tokens / partial-response state, and what signals do we require to avoid double-delivery or lost tokens?

Sam: Short version: either edge retains token/state or we transfer it atomically. both have tradeoffs.

Jordan: +1 on clarifying. Inbound facts: we have KV cache at edge, upstream may also keep a session id. Need clear API for transfer.

Lee: Concern: if edge gives up ownership, billing/observability attribution changes mid-request. who gets the cost and traces?

Maria: Good call — we need a minimal wire contract: transfer semantics + observability headers. I sketched a tiny header set: `X-RI-Resume-Token`, `X-RI-Owner` and `X-RI-Transfer-Id`.

Sam: Can we make transfer id monotonic so retries are idempotent? otherwise hedging causes duplicated transfers.

Jordan: Proposal A (edge-owned): edge keeps token, forwards a blinded token to fallback; fallback cannot finalize without edge confirmation. Pros: single source of truth, easier billing. Cons: edge becomes critical path for resume checks.

Jordan: Proposal B (upstream-owned): atomic transfer RPC: ingress calls `TransferSession(token) -> new_token` and upstream becomes owner. Pros: upstream can evict local caches, simpler resume at upstream. Cons: needs strong ACID-ish handoff or compensating rollback on failure.

Lee: Also think about partial-response semantics. If a fallback returns a partial chunk then upstream later resumes, we must ensure continuity. Need sequence numbers in token.

Sam: Sequence numbers + transfer id seems enough for detect-and-skip duplicates. also, require `Owner` header for billing attribution in traces.

Maria: Operational constraints: our infra prefers edge not to block on round trips >50ms for handoff. so Proposal B requires fast RPC or async commit model.

Jordan: Implementation sketch for atomic RPC (Proposal B):
```
// ingress -> upstream: TransferSession(old_token)
// resp: {new_token, start_seq, transfer_id}
// ingress includes `X-RI-Transfer-Id` when routing subsequent chunks to claim ownership
```
If call fails, ingress retries with exponential backoff and hedges to secondary with same transfer id.

Sam: If hedging, ensure only one upstream can accept a transfer_id. upstreams should respond 409 if transfer_id taken.

Lee: For observability: include `trace.parent=transfer_id` and emit an event `session.transfer` to logs with from/to, transfer_id, latency. helps cost rollup.

Maria: Edge-case: abrupt ingress restart while transfer in-flight. We need a TTL in token and a resurrection policy. default: token expires in 30s and a reclaim endpoint `ReclaimSession(transfer_id)` for admins.

Jordan: Security: tokens must be short-lived signed blobs, not raw offsets. prevents replay if someone routes to wrong cluster.

Sam: Can we agree on minimal required fields for the token: `owner`, `start_seq`, `transfer_id`, `ttl`, `signature`? all base64 json blob.

Lee: Ack but prefer compact binary proto later. base64 json ok for now.

Maria: Next actions: Jordan to draft wire headers + small proto, Sam to write hedging behavior matrix, Lee to add observability events. I'll consolidate into a follow-up RFC. timeline: POC in eng-runtime sprint 3.

ops-bot: Deployment check: no blockers for workspace infra, assigned Jira INFR-452 to Jordan. :white_check_mark:

Maria: Thanks — if anyone sees a hard no on Proposal A vs B, say now. otherwise I'll start drafting RFC with the atomic transfer as primary and edge-owned as fallback option.
